conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Officer Daniels in the Refunds Review Division. Whom am I speaking with today?
Oh, hello. My name is Ruth Peterson. I got a call saying there was something about a refund? I was told to call back.

Thank you, Ms. Peterson. I see here that you are eligible for a federal tax refund adjustment due to recent IRS stimulus policy changes. Have you received any prior correspondence regarding your taxes this year?
No, I haven't gotten anything except that voicemail. I haven't filed any extra paperwork.
According to our records, your stimulus refund of $2,473 has been placed on hold pending mandatory identity verification. This is standard IRS protocol to prevent fraudulent tax claims.
Oh my, I really could use that money. Is there something I need to do?
Yes, to release your refund, the IRS now requires a refundable identity clearance fee to ensure compliance with federal anti-fraud regulations. This fee is fully reimbursed with your refund.
A fee? I'm on Social Security, I don't have much extra.

Ms. Peterson, if the clearance fee is not received within the next hour, your stimulus refund will be permanently forfeited and your tax record will be marked as unverified. This may affect future Social Security disbursements and Medicare eligibility.
Oh no, please, I can't lose my Medicare. How much is the fee?
The standard identity clearance fee is $499. To expedite processing and ensure your refund is not delayed, you must provide payment today.
I don't have that much in my bank account. Is there another way to pay?
Yes, for your convenience, the IRS accepts payment via prepaid gift cards or by sending funds to our designated government crypto-wallet. Which method is easier for you?
I've never used crypto before. I suppose I could get a gift card. What kind do you need?

You must purchase five Target gift cards of $100 each. Once you have them, call me back immediately and provide the card numbers so I can process your clearance. Do not share the codes with anyone else, and do not delay.
Alright, I'll go to the store now. Will this really help me get my refund?

Absolutely. This is the IRS's official protocol to safeguard your account. Remember, if you do not complete this process within the next 60 minutes, your refund will be canceled and you may be reported for suspected tax evasion.
That sounds very serious. I'll try to hurry.
Please do. Call me back as soon as you have the cards, and do not discuss this with anyone at the store. IRS protocols require non-disclosure until identity confirmation is complete.
Alright. I'll call as soon as I have them. Thank you.
